cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Fake the Expertise
cards.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll tune your violin for the audition. I work by ear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've tightened that string until it snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. That string couldn't hold pitch. I've saved you a failure onstage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The audition panel heard it snap. They're asking if you know what you're doing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I rejected an unreliable string. Ask for their spare violin; I'll check that one before I approve it.

mechanism: A claims authority to approve instruments and dismiss questions, turning a tuning failure into evidence of expert quality control.
confusable: Ordinary confidence might deny error; the pair must use approval power to keep directing the audition equipment after exposure.
comparison: Public audition scrutiny and replacement instrument differ from remote engineer question management.
seedUse: D18-b already contains instrument approval and rejection language, so the S01 decision restriction reinforces the existing merged tactic.
